page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. The platform delivers 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at 2.7 GHz, operating without hyperthreading. Memory is configured at 384.0 GB, providing an exact compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes 64 KB L1 data cache and 2 MB L2 cache per core alongside a 36 MB shared L3 cache. It incorporates a 400 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no local storage, and includes no discrete graphics hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel throughput across highly multi-threaded tasks. Multi-core performance under stress-ng places the system in the top tier, matching exceptional results in large-block memory read bandwidth (959.17 GB/s) and write bandwidth (434.92 GB/s). Workloads evaluating software compilation with Clang and ray tracing also test within the highest percentile. Conversely, single-core CPU testing and single-threaded gzip compression register in the middle quartile, indicating that the architecture prioritizes aggregate core density over extreme single-threaded clock frequencies.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the c8gb.48xlarge maximizes compute core allocation per chassis without hyperthreading overhead, enabling consistent, predictable processing for parallel tasks. Storage relies entirely on remote networked volumes, necessitating architecture planning for I/O paths over the 400 Gbps network adapter. The platform is well matched for software build pipelines, distributed batch processing, high-throughput caching applications, and compute-bound simulation services.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gb.48xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized instance driven by 192 dedicated AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 384.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard compute profile of 2.0 GB per core, and is connected via a 400 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance features no bundled local storage and operates without GPU acceleration, relying on remote volumes for persistence. Benchmark metrics highlight exceptional multi-core computational throughput, massive memory bandwidth reaching 959.17 GB/s read, and top-tier performance in distributed caching and software compilation. While single-thread execution rates remain moderate, the architecture delivers consistent multi-threaded compute density. It is specifically suited for high-concurrency workloads, including large-scale CI/CD build environments, compute-heavy simulations, Redis caching nodes, and multi-threaded batch data transformations.
